title: Effect of charge-imbalance potential relaxation on the high-frequency vortex dynamics and kinetic inductance of superconducting circuits
authors: R. I. Kinzibaev, V. S. Stolyarov, A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract: We show that relaxation of the charge-imbalance potential plays a key role in the retarded dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in a type-II superconducting sample carrying a microwave current. Starting from the time-dependent Ginzburg--Landau equations we derive the vortex equation of motion accounting both the dissipation and retardation effects. The retardation is governed by the dynamics of the charge-imbalance potential and reveals itself at characteristic timescales diverging near the superconducting critical temperature $T_{c}$. These retardation effects in vortex dynamics strongly affect the kinetic inductance of superconducting circuits being, thus, responsible for the magnetic field dependence of characteristics of different superconducting devices in the high frequency range.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes vortex motion in superconductors by incorporating the crucial role of charge-imbalance potential relaxation into the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau framework. It derives an advanced equation of motion that captures retardation effects, showing how these mechanisms fundamentally alter the kinetic inductance observed in superconducting circuits at high frequencies.
main_problem: The study investigates how the relaxation of the charge-imbalance potential influences the high-frequency dynamics of Abrikosov vortices in superconducting circuits.
main_result: Retardation effects, governed by this potential relaxation, significantly alter the vortex equation of motion and consequently modify the kinetic inductance of superconducting devices at high frequencies.
method: The analysis utilizes the time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) equations, employing perturbation theory and Fourier transforms to derive frequency-domain equations for vortex velocity and supercurrent density.
model_or_system: The system is a Type-II superconducting sample carrying a microwave current. The model is based on extending the TDGL framework to account for charge-imbalance potential dynamics, which governs the retarded response of vortices.

main_assumptions: The analysis is primarily restricted to gapless superconductors in the dirty limit, and approximations are made regarding the averaging over the vortex lattice.

paper_structure: The paper builds from the fundamental TDGL equations to derive an effective equation of motion for vortex dynamics that incorporates both Ohmic dissipation and retardation effects arising from the charge-imbalance relaxation. This leads to a frequency-dependent impedance calculation affecting $L_k$.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the inclusion of dynamic potential relaxation and resulting frequency-dependent inertia/damping mechanisms provides a rich model for understanding dissipative dynamics in complex quantum systems near phase transitions.
